speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what steps will be taken to ensure that construction on the "Long Island" reclaimed site will not significantly impact sensitive marine habitats like coral reefs; (b) whether a public consultation will be carried out; and (c) whether the nature groups have been or will be consulted from an early stage on this process.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what is the projected environmental impact, specifically concerning marine life and habitats, from the "Long Island" reclamation project; and (b) whether the Government will involve environmental groups and nature researchers in stakeholder consultations to assess and mitigate potential ecological consequences before commencing the project.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: asked the Minister for National Development in relation to the "Long Island" project (a) what have been the considerations for population and developmental planning along East Coast Parkway; (b) what is the longer-term impact on property prices in the area; and (c) whether significant traffic infrastructures will be required to facilitate smooth traffic flow adjoining the areas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I invite the Member to seek clarifications if need be.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If the question has been addressed, it may not be necessary to proceed with the question for future Sittings.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These studies will take into account surrounding marine habitats, including intertidal flats and coral communities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked about the considerations for and the impact of the planned developments at East Coast Parkway and "Long Island".

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It offers an integrated solution to meet the multiple needs of future generations, including the building of new homes with a quality living environment, comprising coastal and reservoir parks and amenities, as well as creating new jobs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: By reclaiming "Long Island" away from the current coastline, we can achieve coastal protection, the strengthening of our water supply and creation of new tracts of land, while retaining the existing East Coast Park largely as it is.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are only at the very beginning of the process – kickstarting environmental and engineering studies to determine feasibility, as well as the shape and form of "Long Island".

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At a later stage, agencies will undertake further studies to ensure that the area is well developed – with quality housing, network of new green spaces integrated with East Coast Park and good transport connectivity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We recognise that many people and stakeholders would be keen to understand and know more about the project and how it may potentially impact them – residents, businesses, nature and heritage groups, the sporting and water sports community, park users, maritime industry and many more groups.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That is why we are starting our planning and engagement early.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim asked about the source of reclamation sand.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The import of reclamation sand to Singapore is conducted on a commercial basis and sand is imported from a variety of sources.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Importers must abide by the laws and regulations of source countries.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These include sourcing from legally permissible areas, obtaining the proper export documentation and permits from the relevant authorities, as well as complying with local environmental regulations governing proper extraction and transport within source countries.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Where applicable, our agencies would check that the necessary environmental-related approvals from the source countries are in order before contractors are allowed to commence sand imports.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think there is particular concern about the source of the sand that we are using for this project.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Minister has clarified some of the questions about this earlier.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But could I ask, one, whether we have a list of countries where we are hoping to import sand from; and two, whether we will have a responsible sourcing framework to evaluate the social and environmental impact of the imported sand?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We must ensure that as much as we study the impact of our "Long Island" plans on our own surroundings and environment, we also want to make sure that when we import material for reclamation and other works, that our commercial operators also act within the ambit of the laws and regulations of the source countries and minimise the impact of their operations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The list of countries where we import from, some of these are available online in terms of the quantity of sand.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But when we are talking about "Long Island", this is far into the future.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Works are not going to proceed in the near term.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, this will be something that will be developed as the technical studies and implementation plans get greater granularity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If I may just push a little bit, my understanding is that this sand is typically procured by JTC Corporation – I am willing to stand corrected on that.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: What are the mechanisms to ensure that JTC complies with the stipulations that the Ministry sets forth?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And secondly, if I may just follow up from the Member Louis Ng's question: what is the broader framework?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I think what we want to avoid is a situation where we get just all the valid paperwork, but we violate the spirit of acquiring sand in an ethical fashion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And I think that is, ultimately, what he may be suggesting when it comes to a broader framework for acquisition of sand.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I think the Member made very sensible points, along with Member Louis Ng.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And the source countries will have their own regulators.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But on Singapore's end, the entity that procures the sand will, where necessary, do the necessary checks to ensure that the rules and regulations and the paperwork are in compliance.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Can I ask the Minister, when are the environmental studies going to be commenced and how long would they be expected to take?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I think the Minister mentioned earlier that there are some checks that are done by the agencies with their counterparts overseas, from source countries, on where the sand comes from.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I just want to understand, how often are these checks done and what triggers their being carried out; whether it is through tip-offs or whether it is a regular spot check or audit?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: How do they actually decide when to carry out these checks to make sure that all the regulations have been complied with?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And then, the follow-on thought process from that is, whether or not our current regime is strict and enough to make sure that all these things, like illegal mining and smuggling of sand, do not take place as and when our counterparts export the sand to us?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I have got two supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: The first one is with regard to the population.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: While there is reclamation and there will be additional land mass at the area, I think the East Coast residents would be concerned, partly because there is already a Bayshore Build-To-Order (BTO) project that is upcoming.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: While the "Long Island" project may be decades out, it would increase the entire population around the area.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: So, that is the reason behind my question.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: What is the population framework control that is thought behind this?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: The second supplementary question is, the Minister has explained that this entire project planning and implementation will take several decades.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: So, the whole idea is there will be newer technologies around coastal protection that may come up over time.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: How are we going to integrate some of these newer technologies, in terms of the protection around the "Long Island" project or along the East Coast, so that we will not just put all the expenditure only on one project, particularly around the "Long Island" project?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This came out in the latest report, version 3 of Singapore's National Climate Change study.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And if it coincides with storm surges and high tide, by as much as four to five metres.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, certainly with some one-third of Singapore's land being below five metres above mean sea level, this is an existential challenge.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And not doing anything about it is not an option.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the same time, we have to plan early and well in advance, harnessing the various technologies that are available to tackle sea level rise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When we did the site-specific study, we focused on areas which face some of the greatest risks of flood inundation from sea level rise.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We started with the city to the East Coast; we are also working on Jurong Island, the Jurong West area and also the northwestern coast.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: When we did the study for City-East Coast, essentially, the broad mitigation measures revolved around two possible measures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One was the "Long Island", where you reclaim and build land higher at the distance from the existing coast.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, this is, effectively, the indicative plan for the "Long Island" reclamation profile for coastal protection.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The specific technologies – whether you are pumping, whether you have coastal walls, whether you have nature-based solutions incorporated – these are the technical details that will be studied over the course of the next five years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, that is in response to the Member's second question.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In response to the first question, starting from this year, we will engage all stakeholders, all Singaporeans, including residents that the Member has spoken about, who are concerned about the plans for the future "Long Island".

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As part of the Draft Master Plan 2025, we consult Singaporeans on the detailed concepts and ideas around various parts of Singapore, flowing through from the Long-Term Plan or Concept Plan which we concluded two years ago in 2022 and 2023.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In terms of the master planning of the future land that will be generated over the course of the decades ahead of us as we implement the "Long Island" project, that will be subject to detailed planning; and certainly, detailed consultation with stakeholders, including the Member's residents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: If I could go back just to the issue of sand again.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I understand that with the sand imports, we are reliant on compliance with the local laws, but I think the concern is that the local laws might not be as strong as we hope for them to be.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: And so, the call is for our own responsible sourcing framework, and for this framework to be made public as well, so that we are assured that the import of the sand will not affect the social and environmental conditions in other countries.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Certainly, we have a mechanism in place in the contractual procurement processes, to ensure that rules and regulations are complied with.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Certainly, the source countries have their own rules that they implement to protect their local communities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And we will certainly continue to find ways to continue to improve the processes, so that we ensure that the sourcing is done well and that the environmental impact here in Singapore is also mitigated.
